themes.title: Far-Right Surge in European Regional Elections and Governance
themes.blurb: Right-wing nationalist parties across Western and Central Europe are capitalizing on high polling momentum to demand direct governing roles or celebrate unprecedented administrative stability. From state elections in East Germany to coalition power dynamics in Scandinavia, populist movements are positioning themselves as central governing authorities rather than peripheral protest movements.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: Leading polls at 42-43% in Saxony-Anhalt ahead of Sunday's vote, threatening a historic absolute majority and the collapse of the CDU political firewall.

countries.name: 🇸🇪 Sverigedemokraterna
countries.note: Asserting influence over the Tidö coalition while demanding up to 12-14 ministerial posts in the next government formation.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Giorgia Meloni and her coalition partners mark 1,413 days in power, establishing the longest-serving uninterrupted government in Italy's post-war republican history.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: Marine Le Pen maintains strong polling leads for the 2027 presidential race while securing over 400 official candidate sponsorships.

countries.name: 🇳🇴 Fremskrittspartiet
countries.note: Surging to become Norway's largest party in national polls at 31.4%, eclipsing both the governing Labour Party and Conservatives.

themes.title: Immigration and Border Security as Political Wedges
themes.blurb: Right-wing parties across Europe are using territorial border friction and migration influxes to weaponize national security concerns against incumbent governments. Recent border tensions in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta have become a focal point for coordinated messaging across Spanish, Italian, and French nationalist movements.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Organizing nationwide protests and EU demonstrations over the Ceuta migrant crisis, framing the influx as Moroccan 'hybrid warfare'.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Lega lawmakers visited Ceuta to demand EU border enforcement while Matteo Salvini pushed for aggressive municipal migrant crackdowns in Naples.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: Focusing state election debates on rapid mass deportations, abolishing asylum rights, and barring foreign workers.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: Denouncing 'forced immigration' and using border crises to advocate for strict European frontier controls.

countries.name: 🇸🇪 Sverigedemokraterna
countries.note: Partnering with the government to roll out expanded emergency measures against criminal migrant networks and urban integration issues.

themes.title: Populist Right Battles Media Bias and Digital Censorship
themes.blurb: Right-wing political figures and movements are intensifying their offensive against established news outlets and public broadcasting structures. From legal interventions in tech copyright disputes to threats of defunding state broadcasters, conservative actors frame existing media entities as ideologically hostile.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: The administration intervened in court to back OpenAI against The New York Times while Trump threatened regulatory actions against major television networks.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: Pledging to terminate the state contract for public broadcaster MDR in Saxony-Anhalt, condemning state media as a threat to democracy.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: Nigel Farage attacked public broadcasters, accusing news organizations of fabricating conspiracy theories regarding party funding sources.

countries.name: 🇭🇺 Fidesz / Tisza
countries.note: Contesting oversight and appointment rules for the Independent Public Media Authority ahead of national broadcasting restructuring.

themes.title: Nationalist Symbolism and Rebranding of Public Institutions
themes.blurb: Populist and nationalist leaders are systematically utilizing physical monuments, institutional symbolism, and sovereign infrastructure to project power and cement historical legacies. Government executive actions are increasingly focused on physically redesigning public spaces or asserting national control over disputed sites.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: Issuing $1 coins depicting Donald Trump's face, advancing plans for a White House ballroom, and proposing interstate highways named in his honor.

countries.name: 🇦🇷 La Libertad Avanza
countries.note: Announcing a national naval base project in Tierra del Fuego to physically reinforce sovereignty claims over the Falkland Islands.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Hosting major public gatherings at port facilities in Bari to celebrate government longevity and commemorate historical right-wing icons.

countries.name: 🇭🇺 Fidesz / Tisza
countries.note: Revoking special designations and oversight structures for major public campus developments and state-backed cultural projects.

themes.title: Economic Nationalism and Trade Disputes
themes.blurb: Right-wing agendas are increasingly prioritizing domestic energy extraction, industrial protectionism, and aggressive posture in international trade conflicts. Parties argue that globalist environmental regulations and foreign trade reliance severely handicap national industries.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: Escalating trade war rhetoric against Canadian imports, lifting beef tariff limits, and securing bilateral energy access in South America.

countries.name: 🇦🇷 La Libertad Avanza
countries.note: Pushing the Súper RIGI economic reform bill through Congress with local supplier mandates while spending on foreign defense acquisitions.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: Demanding unrestricted North Sea oil and gas expansion and promising the total repeal of net-zero energy levies.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: Attacking green transition policies and Russian sanctions, linking EV mandates directly to major domestic automotive plant closures.
